newsitem.title: CANADA: Volvo said interested in Quebec bus maker.
newsitem.headline: Volvo said interested in Quebec bus maker.

text.p: Swedish car maker AB Volvo is among several large European and U.S. companies interested in acquiring Quebec bus manufacturer Nova Bus Corp, an official of the Quebec Federation of Labour said.

"It is no secret. Volvo is involved with Nova Bus," Quebec Federation of Labour official Louis Fournier told Reuters. The Federation, one of Quebec's largest trade unions, has a 19 percent stake in Nova Bus.

Industry sources and Canadian newspapers have reported that Germany's Daimler-Benz AG and Scania AK are among several foreign companies currently performing due diligence with an eye to acquiring Nova Bus.
"Five companies are interested in Nova. Among them, three are European and two are from the United States. It is easy to know who they are," said Fournier.
Nova Bus confirmed it had received approaches from several interested buyers, but declined to name the companies involved.

"I cannot confirm the names of the players because of a confidentiality agreement. I can tell you that 12 companies were interested at the beginning but now only three of them are serious contenders," said Nova Bus spokesman Jean-FrancoisLebrun.

He denied news reports in Montreal's La Presse and Toronto's Financial Post saying that formal bids were about to be made. "There has been no formal offer with numbers and figures. We are not about to conclude," Lebrun told Reuters.

Montreal-based Nova Bus Corp designs and manufactures urban transit buses in North America. The company, in which Canadian aircraft and rail car manufacturer Bombardier Inc has a 25 percent shareholding, has revenues of C$450 million and more than 1,700 employees in Canada, the United States and Mexico.
It made large sales to transit authorities in Toronto, New York City, Dallas and Santa Barbara, California.
Bombardier and Volvo declined to comment on the reports. "We don't comment on speculation," Volvo official Mats Edenborg told Reuters.
Volvo is the world's second biggest bus maker and is reported to be building up its market position in North America after the 1995 acquisition of Quebec's Prevost Car Inc for C$140 million.
Located near Quebec City. Prevost Car builds urban transit buses for the North American market. It has 1,200 employees.
Both Bombardier and Volvo declined to comment on the reports. "We don't comment on speculation," Volvo official Mats Edenborg told Reuters.
